subject: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows

messages.author: 3f3ab1c76618502a
messages.subject: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows
parts:
Under Windows, I get a runtime error R6034 when I open any R file in gVim. Fortunately, after I dismiss the error everything works fine! Surely this error is not caused by the plugin, but by one of the components it uses (pywin32 is my guess). However, I would really appreciate any help I can get in solving it.

I followed the installation instructions for Windows carefully, making sure I have the right versions of each required software. I have:

- Vim 7.4
- R version 3.0.3
- vimcom.plus version 0.9-93
- Python 2.7.6 (32 bit)
- pywin32-218.win32-py2.7.exe
- Windows 7 pro SP1 64-bit

I searched for a solution but to no avail. I found this:

https://code.google.com/p/vim/issues/detail?id=173

suggesting something about python loading the MSVC runtime DLL without having a correct manifest? I don't really understand what that means. On a different machine, also with Windows 7, it did work without this error, albeit with older versions of some of the programs (vim 7.3, python 2.7.3), so I'm not sure that my problem is related to this.

Thanks, any help appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows
parts:
If you are getting Windows error r6034 which is a runtime error then it means that some files of windows are missing such as dll files, windows driver, registry file etc. If system is not well configured then you may also receive runtime error r6034 so you need to system restore, system repair, update windows, windows driver, scan the system and remove malicious programs if any found, before installing any software or hardware be sure that it is compatible with your system . If you follow the given answers then you can fix runtime error r6034. If you need more help then visit the given link:
http://www.removewindowserror.com

messages.subject: Re: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows
parts:
Hi,

I haven't been using the plugin under Windows, because I prefer to use Tinn-R on this OS.
Additionally, I have used much more Linux than Windows.

To do tests it was installed a fresh version of Vim (7.4), the stable version of the Vim-R-plugin and its dependencies (see plugin doc).
I found the same problem when opening any R extension covered by the plugin.

Web search led me to this link: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9764341/runtime-error-with-vim-omnicompletion
Following the instructions it was possible to remove the error message.

You will need of the small (and free) program mt.exe. I found it here: http://originaldll.com/file/mt.exe/21861.html

Copy it to the folder where gvim was installed and follows the instructions of the link.

Notice: 
- It was necessary to change the privileges of the main folder where Vim was installed): C:\Program files (x86)\Vim
- it is necessary to create manually both empty files: gvim.manifest and python.manifest.

Attached my final version of gvim.manifest.

HTH,
J.C.Faria
